-- How Lies Kill -- 2 articles

California NORML Press Release Dec. 15, 1998 –

Patient Who Was Denied Liver Transplant For Using Medical Marijuana Dies

California NORML is sorry to note the death of Ed Plotner, who was removed from a liver transplant list for using medical marijuana. Plotner, who suffered multiple hepatitis infections, had used marijuana to combat severe appetite and weight loss. He was accepted, but then dropped by a liver transplant program, which demanded that he pass a drug test for marijuana. Unlike other drugs, including cocaine, heroin, and alcohol, marijuana is not a risk factor for hepatitis.

Even though many patients find medical marijuana is useful - not only for weight gain, but also for helping them to avoid drugs that are toxic to the liver -- - it is banned in most transplant programs. California NORML attorney Eric Shevin attempted to get Plotner restored to the transplant list, but his efforts proved too late. After being kept off the list a year, Ed expired on November 21.

"Ed was a tragic victim of drug testing abuse," says California NORML coordinator Dale Gieringer, "He was killed by the anti-marijuana bigotry and ignorance of medical ‘experts’ who should have known better." Ironically, Plotner, who was from Redding, Cal., had sought treatment in San Francisco, where voters overwhelmingly approved medical marijuana by 80% to 20%. ***Dale Gieringer (415) 563-5858 //

December 10, 1998
From the Tucson Citizen
letters@tucsoncitizen.com
http://www.tucsoncitizen.com/
By Ronald R. Watson

Letters To The Editor

MARIJUANA SUPPRESSES HEALTH

Marijuana is addictive and very toxic.

See
The Relative Addictiveness of Drugs According to NIDA's Own Researcher

When physicians go outside their area of expertise and research, they frequently make mistakes.
(Marijuananews note: Precisely, but it is not at all clear to me what this man’s "area of expertise" might be. It certainly is not "logical thought.")

Thus Dr. Andrew Weil, who has contributed so much to the wise use of plants in medicine, was dead wrong when he said that marijuana is "one of the safest drugs known to medicine."
See

More than a decade ago my research lab found that the addictive component of marijuana, THC, suppressed the human immune system required for optimum cancer and disease resistance.
(Marijuananews note: The "addictive component," THC, is sold with FDA approval as Marinol.
See
Two Days After The Medical Marijuana Initiatives
The DEA Proposes Making Marinol A Schedule III Drug!! "Like Codeine With Tylenol."
More Like Cynicism With Desperation
and

Not unexpectedly many researchers have found that regular smoking of marijuana, like tobacco smoke, by humans and animals greatly increases lung disease and oral cancer.
(Marijuananews note: There is simply no such research regarding cancer. There is some research showing an increase in respiratory problems among heavy smokers. The recent Lancet article on the adverse effects of cannabis said, "In 1997, Tashkin and colleagues reported that the rate of decline in respiratory function over 8 years among marijuana smokers did not differ from that in non-smokers. This finding contrasted with that of a follow-up of the Tucson cohort, in which there was a greater rate of decline in respiratory function among marijuana-only smokers than in tobacco-only smokers and additive effects of tobacco and marijuana smoking. Both studies showed that long-term cannabis smoking increased bronchitic symptoms.")
See
A Mediocre Review Called The "Adverse Effects of Cannabis" Published In The Lancet

Marijuana smoking is no more dangerous than tobacco. But tobacco kills 500,000 Americans a year. How can it be a "safe drug?"
(Marijuananews note: This has absolutely no bearing on the relative safety of the medicl use of marijuana or any other drug. Opiate abuse kills people, but opiates are used in medicine.)

Happily federal restrictions have kept the regular use of marijuana down, saving thousands of lives.
(Marijuananews note: In vitro research and reviewing prohibitionist propaganda does not make a person an expert on the consequences of a given public policy.)
See
Legalize Marijuana and Reduce Use?
New Survey Puts Estimate of Dutch Marijuana Use Even More Below DEAland

Daily exposure to environmental, tobacco or marijuana smoke similarly cause many lung and systemic medical problems.

(Marijuananews note: There is no evidence that second hand marijuana smoke causes any health problems, simply because there is so little of it, both research and second hand marijuana smoke.)

The Citizen could do a service to the Tucson public by interviewing local marijuana researchers on its toxic properties.

(Marijuananews note: Of course, they would have to ignore the Lancet, etc. Is science now local? No, just bad "science.")

Ronald R. Watson
Professor of public health research
Arizona Prevention Center
